title: Top 2 products per category
summary: The classic report: the best sellers in every category, ties included.
prompt: Merchandising wants the **two best-selling products in each category** by units sold.

Return `category`, `product` and `units` (total units sold), for every product whose rank inside its category is 1 or 2. **Ties share a rank** and are all included (so a category can return three rows when two products tie for second).
Products that never sold are not in the report. Order by `category`, then `units` descending, then `product`.
setup: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE order_lines (order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER REFERENCES products(id), qty INTEGER NOT NULL);
solution: SELECT p.category, p.name AS product, SUM(l.qty) AS units
FROM products p JOIN order_lines l ON l.product_id = p.id
SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC) AS r FROM sold
SELECT category, product, units FROM ranked WHERE r <= 2
ORDER BY category, units DESC, product;
wrong: SELECT p.category, p.name AS product, SUM(l.qty) AS units
FROM products p JOIN order_lines l ON l.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY units DESC LIMIT 2;
WITH sold AS (SELECT p.category, p.name AS product, SUM(l.qty) AS units FROM products p JOIN order_lines l ON l.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id),
ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC) AS r FROM sold)
SELECT category, product, units FROM ranked WHERE r <= 2 ORDER BY category, units DESC, product;
hints: Total the units per product first (a CTE), then rank inside each category.
`RANK()` gives ties the same rank; `ROW_NUMBER()` would drop one of them.
You cannot filter on a window function in `WHERE` of the same SELECT: wrap it in another CTE.
